claims.statement: The async get_agent(config) factory in agent/server.py compiles the primary coding agent for an executable thread run by resolving its sandbox, model policy, tool surface, subagent, skills, and middleware before calling create_deep_agent.

get_agent returns a bare create_deep_agent with empty system prompt and no tools, sandbox, or supplied middleware when there is no thread_id or the load is not for execution, gated by graph_loaded_for_execution reading the __is_for_execution__ configurable flag.

get_agent starts a cached SandboxBackendProxy for the thread with a reconnect callback that builds a LocalShellBackend for desktop runs and otherwise calls ensure_sandbox_for_thread with the selected environment.

The main and subagent model settings resolve in get_agent by precedence: team defaults, dashboard profile overrides, stored thread settings, then an explicit per-run agent_model_id and agent_effort validated against SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS and model_supports_effort.

construct_system_prompt renders the per-thread main-agent template with optional source, plan, repository, environment, and admin sections, while render_open_swe_shared_base appends the static OPEN_SWE_SHARED_BASE with conditional sandbox-download guidance.

The CompositeBackend overlays bundled skills from a read-only FilesystemBackend, hosted organization and credential-owner user skills from read-only StoreBackends, and desktop user skills from a read-only StateBackend; its ordered skill_sources list is shared with the general-purpose subagent.

The configured general-purpose subagent compiles independently of parent middleware, so it carries its own dynamic-tool and exclusion middleware, workflow-push guard, and model guards including SanitizeOpenAIResponsesMiddleware and ModelCallTimeoutMiddleware.

The main agent's middleware list is ordered outermost to innermost with preparation and policy guards outside model sanitizers and ModelCallTimeoutMiddleware innermost, so the provider deadline can escalate outward to the fallback model.

PlanModeMiddleware is installed unconditionally with the factory's initial configurable plan_mode value, resets state to that value at run start, and filters each model request so a mid-run enter_plan_mode command restricts the next turn without leaking stale plan mode into a later run.

PrepareAgentRunMiddleware appends sender identity, attribution, user instructions, and participant context as a separate generated context message after a human input, rather than rewriting the authored message or placing that context in the durable system prompt.

ensure_sandbox_for_thread does not replace an unreachable existing sandbox by default because that may lose uncommitted work, but it replaces a deleted sandbox so the thread is not permanently bound to a stale id.

The graph is registered as agent.graphs.agent:traced_agent, which exports get_agent, and get_agent binds its result with a config stripped of __pregel_* runtime internals to avoid serializing a read-time runtime into later calls.

RunConfig treats configurable as a tolerant cross-launcher contract: declared fields are optional, unknown keys are retained, and parsing removes invalid fields individually rather than discarding the rest of the configuration.

Hosted assembly persists the resolved main/subagent settings and repository instructions before applying the Fable availability gate; model construction failures become deferred error models, and fallback middleware is installed only for a different model id.

BasePrepareRunMiddleware checkpoints per-run setup with a fingerprint of middleware type, latest message, and configuration; retries before checkpoint persistence require preparation to be idempotent, while later invocations re-prepare fresh context.

Desktop runs route Deep Agents' virtual /large_tool_results/ and /conversation_history directories to a thread-specific artifact root outside the selected repository so offloads do not become git changes.

DynamicToolMiddleware resets integration selections at each run start, requires load_integration_tools before an integration tool call, serializes each group's construction, converts failures into unavailable-tool results, and rejects collisions with reserved names.

When plan mode is active, its exclusion set removes task delegation and selected external mutation, but leaves file editing and execute available; excluding task prevents delegation to an independently compiled subagent from bypassing the parent restriction.

The parent static tool surface is conditional: trusted Slack context enables Slack tools, authorized admin threads add ADMIN_TOOLS, desktop and stop-summary runs use restricted lists, and ExcludeToolsMiddleware applies normal or stop-summary Deep Agent exclusions.

Input-message serialization requires namespaced sender identifiers, wraps authored human or system content in structured input-message envelopes, and deduplicates content-addressed dynamic introductions while allowing hidden summarized context to be reintroduced.
Credential-scope lookup failure does not abort graph assembly; it marks the scope unknown and omits hosted MCP and Notion tools instead of assuming personal-integration authority.

Adaptive model routing is enabled from the applicable profile or team policy unless snapshotted in thread settings, creates fast, balanced, and performance routing models, and records the applied decision in metadata.

Focused assembly tests verify backend and skills routes, credential-scope behavior, desktop and stop-summary tool surfaces, Slack/admin gates, parent-only subagent tools, plan exclusions, middleware ordering, and concurrent MCP/Notion loading.
